Retries and backoff

tinyqueue is a small job queue for Node.js. This page explains how a failed job is retried, and how to change the delay between attempts.

On this page

  • Default behavior
  • Configuring retries
  • Errors that skip retries
  • Questions

Default behavior

A job that throws is retried up to 3 times. The wait before each attempt doubles, starting at 500 milliseconds. After the final failure the job moves to the failed list, where you can inspect it with tinyqueue inspect.

import { Queue } from 'tinyqueue';

const queue = new Queue('emails');

queue.process(async (job) => {
  await sendEmail(job.data.to, job.data.subject);
});

Configuring retries

Pass a retry object when you add a job. Every field is optional, and a field you leave out keeps its default.

await queue.add(
  { to: 'ada@example.org', subject: 'Welcome to the course' },
  { retry: { attempts: 5, delay: 1000, factor: 2, maxDelay: 60000, jitter: true } },
);

With these values the waits are one, two, four, eight and sixteen seconds, each shifted slightly at random so that many failing jobs do not retry at the same moment.

Reading the job's history

Each attempt is recorded. Print the log with:

$ tinyqueue history 4821
attempt 1  failed  ECONNRESET  after 12 ms
attempt 2  failed  ECONNRESET  after 9 ms
attempt 3  done    ok          after 41 ms

Errors that skip retries

Some failures will never succeed on a second try. Throw an UnrecoverableError and tinyqueue moves the job to failed straight away.

Which built-in errors are unrecoverable?

Validation errors, missing handlers and malformed payloads. Network errors and timeouts are always retried.

Can I retry a failed job by hand?

Yes. Run tinyqueue retry 4821, or call job.retry() from your own code. The attempt counter starts again from one.

Questions

Does a retry keep the original job id?

Yes. Retries reuse the id, so anything that tracks the job by id keeps working.

Is there a limit on the delay?

Set maxDelay to cap it. Without a cap the delay keeps growing with each attempt.
